thread:
DevOps-Bot: INCIDENT ALERT: High tail latency observed for /v1/generate (p95=420ms, p99=2.8s) — paging oncall (severity: P1)
Ari: ack — paging in. seeing this in prod across two regions?
Sam: yep eu-west and us-west both show p99 spikes around same epoch, error rates stable but timeouts rising. customer-facing requests timed out a few times.
Maya: adding context — we rolled continuous-batching change last night to tighten batch window. Might be related.
Jordan: FYI the KV-cache mem usage jumped ~3x in last 30m on multiple pods, eviction rates up. logs show repeated cache key churn.
Ari: @Sam can you grab trace for a single slow request? want to see if it's batching or model-side.
Sam: attaching trace snippet: ```span:client->gateway 5ms; gateway->runtime 2100ms wait; runtime exec 40ms; runtime wait for kvcache 2000ms``` looks like runtime waiting on cache loads.
Lee: that's consistent with cache blowups — cache misses causing synchronous disk/remote fetches. continuous batching could be expanding KV working set causing thrash.
Maya: paging question — any customer impact? Which customers hit 504s?
Sam: a few mid-tier customers reported single-request timeouts, SLOs degraded but no total outage. Support already notified.
Ari: ok immediate mitigation options: 1) disable continuous batching to fall back to time-window batching, 2) increase KV cache TTL/size to reduce churn, 3) temporarily raise HPA min replicas to absorb extra latency. Which is least risky?
Jordan: disable continuous batching first — simple config flip via rollout (no model change). I can push a patch.
Maya: +1 do that and also set cache eviction to aggressive soft-protect? might be risky.
Lee: increasing cache size in prod is slower (requires node restart in private), not great for immediate. HPA bump is fastest — scale to minReplicas=6 from 3 to give headroom. But watch thrash: if we keep batching high, HPA can overshoot and cause warmup issues.
Ari: plan: Jordan flips continuous-batching -> off; Lee increases HPA min to 6; Sam monitors latency and KV metrics. If no improvement in 10m, revert KV configs next.
Jordan: applying patch now. rollout id: r-2024-11-05-cb-off
Jordan: ```kubectl set env deployment/runtime CONTINUOUS_BATCHING=false --namespace=prod; kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime```
DevOps-Bot: Deploy started: r-2024-11-05-cb-off by Jordan.
Sam: HPA patch: ```kubectl patch hpa runtime-hpa -p '{"spec": {"minReplicas": 6}}'``` applied.
DevOps-Bot: HPA updated: runtime-hpa minReplicas=6
(3m later)
Sam: initial signals: p99 dropped from 2.8s -> 1.1s within 90s. KV cache miss rate down ~40%. error rates steady.
Maya: support update prepared: "We've mitigated the elevated latency by changing batching config and scaling service; we're monitoring and will follow up once fully stable." Send now?
Ari: send. Also annotate incident timeline.
Jordan: rollback note: if latency doesn't stabilize in 15m we'll re-enable CB with reduced max_batch_size and enable prefix-KV pinning.
Lee: watch HPA CPU and request metrics — if we keep minReplicas high longer than necessary it'll cost a lot and could trigger autoscaling jitter when we scale down. Add warmup annotation: scaleDownCooldownSeconds=300.
Sam: setting annotation now. ```kubectl annotate deployment/runtime autoscaler.k8s.io/scale-down-cooldown="300"```
Ari: good. Also let's throttle internal batch window to 25ms when we re-enable to avoid large batches building up quickly.
(10m later)
Sam: p99 stabilized ~700-900ms — acceptable for now. Customer ticket count decreased. KV cache memory plateaued.
Maya: recommend postmortem: root cause likely interaction between continuous-batching expansion and KV cache footprint growth leading to cache thrash and synchronous remote fetches; that triggered latency cliffs which then fed into HPA decisions.
Jordan: action items: 1) create canary test for continuous-batching enabling to simulate cache working set growth, 2) add safeguard: if KV cache miss rate > 10% for 5m, automatic CB throttle, 3) add HPA smoothing (increase stabilizationWindowSeconds to 180s).
Lee: I'll take HPA smoothing and annotation work. Jordan you own CB canary. Sam/Maya write customer impact blurb + timeline. Ari will own postmortem.
DevOps-Bot: Incident resolved: mitigation in place, monitoring ongoing. Severity reduced to P2.
Ari: handoff to follow-on shift — @Sam please leave a short summary in #incidents and link to runbook updates. I'm off in 30m, @Maya take over if anything flares.
Maya: ack, will monitor. adding follow-ups to backlog.
Sam: summary (for #incidents): "Brief: p99 latency spike caused by KV cache thrash after continuous-batching change; mitigated by disabling continuous-batching and increasing HPA minReplicas; follow-ups include canary tests, throttle safeguards, and HPA smoothing. No major customer data loss; some request timeouts observed."
Ari: thanks team. closing thread unless new alerts come in. :white_check_mark:
